info.title: Busbar administrative API — 1.6.0 additive operations
info.description:
The operations 1.6.0 adds to the administrative surface, described in a document of their own.

This is not a replacement for `GET /api/v1/admin/openapi.json`, and it does not repeat a single path from it. That document describes the 66 operations the 1.5.5 tag pinned and its bytes are fixed: a client that fetched it before the upgrade and after it receives the same bytes, so nothing which reads it can be surprised by a path it does not know. The new operations are reached by asking for this document, at `GET /api/v1/admin/ledger/openapi.json`, by name.

Scope: the five read-only ledger views. The 1.6.0 money-governance verbs (`adjust`, `approve`, `resolve_dispute` and the rest of that set) are deliberately absent — their HTTP bindings are not yet fixed, and describing a binding this document is not entitled to fix would make the document wrong rather than incomplete.

How figures are typed. Every money figure is a JSON string holding a decimal integer, and every count is a JSON number. The ledger keeps money in 128-bit integers; JSON's number is a double, exact only to 2^53, and a nano-unit total passes that on a busy day. A figure that silently lost its last digits would still look like money, so money is carried as text and the reader does the arithmetic.

Authorization. Every operation here is a read and requires the `read-only` scope — the same scope, presented the same way, as the legacy `GET /api/v1/admin/usage` that reads the same money from the other side.

tags.name: ledger
tags.description: Read-only views of what the ledger holds.

get.summary: What the ledger posted, per bucket, day, lane and provider.
get.description: The row width is the reconciliation's row width, so a discrepancy found on one endpoint can be looked up on the other by the same four-part name.

200.description: The rows, in bucket, day, lane and provider order.

get.description: A checkpoint's `body_hash` is what an auditor re-derives independently; `body_hash_verifies` is this node's own answer to the same question. Both are served so the two can be compared rather than one trusted. A signature's presence is reported and its bytes are not: a checkpoint nobody signed and a checkpoint whose signature this response withheld would otherwise look the same.

get.summary: The residual of the ledger's postings against the previous release's rows.
get.description: For every row either side carries, two figures have to agree: the ledger's summed priced amount projected once to micro-units against the row's spend, and the ledger's summed fee count against the row's billable requests. They are checked separately because they fail separately. An empty `discrepancies` list with `holds: true` is the good answer; a residual names the row it is about and the amount it is out by, and its sign says which side is missing it.

200.description: Whether the identity holds, and every row on which it does not.

get.summary: The marker the first boot after the upgrade sealed.
get.description: `migrated` is a field of its own rather than something a reader infers from a null marker, because the two questions an operator is asking — whether this deployment has opened its balances, and what it opened them at — fail separately.

200.description: Whether this deployment has migrated, and the marker if it has.

get.description: Served verbatim from the committed artefact, so the description an operator reads and the description the repository reviews are the same bytes.

adminToken.description: The administrative credential, presented exactly as every legacy admin operation takes it.

Unauthenticated.description: No credential, or one the node does not recognise.

Forbidden.description: A credential that does not hold the scope this operation requires.

Amount.description: A money figure as a decimal integer in text. See the document description for why money is not a JSON number.

bucket.description: Whose budget the usage was attributed to.

day.description: The UTC-day bucket, as the unix second it opens at.

lane.description: The serving lane's configured model name.

priced_nanos.description: The summed post-tier priced amount of every posting on this row, in nano-units.

priced_micros.description: The same figure in micro-units: ONE truncating divide over the summed nano-units, never a sum of per-posting divides.

fee_count.description: One per billable client request on this row.

wall.description: When it was sealed, in whole seconds.

body_hash_verifies.description: This node's own answer to whether the sealed body re-hashes to `body_hash`.

signed.description: Whether a signature is present. The signature's bytes are never served.

window.description: The window's opening instant, in whole seconds.

holds.description: True when every row reconciles. `discrepancies` is then empty.

ledger_fee_count.description: What the ledger's postings charged fees for on this row.

legacy_billable_requests.description: What the previous release's row says was billable.

accounted.description: Where the value the ledger drew is now.

drawn.description: What the previous release's row records as taken.

amount.description: `accounted` minus `drawn`. Zero is the good answer; the sign says which side is missing the difference.

balances.description: How many balances the opening carries.

cells_read.description: How many of the previous release's cells were read to arrive at them.

rate_card_version.description: Which card version the opening entries were priced under.
